title: Why I still draw with a pencil
excerpt: Pencil and charcoal portraits, and what they teach me about looking.

blocks.text:
Sample entry, written to show the design. Replace it with your own words in Pages CMS, or delete it.

Most of my drawings are portraits in pencil and charcoal. A pencil is slow, and that's the point: it makes me look properly at light, shape and expression.

Faces first

A face asks for patience: the light on a cheek, the weight of a look, the line that changes the whole expression. That way of looking stays with me in everything else I make.

A portrait is finished when it looks back at you.
